options: Running tasks at the very same moment on different cores
Switching between tasks on one worker
Writing code that has no loops
check.explanation: Parallelism needs more than one core running work at once. Switching on one worker is concurrency.
check.hint: Is anything literally happening at the same moment?

check.prompt: Two tasks both add 1 to a shared counter at the same time and one update is lost. What is this called?
check.explanation: When the result depends on the exact timing of tasks sharing data, you have a race condition.
check.hint: The result depends on who gets there first.

options: Concurrency always makes a program faster
A program can be concurrent on a single core
check.explanation: A single core can switch between tasks, which is concurrency. Parallelism needs several cores, and concurrency alone does not guarantee speed.
check.hint: Can one worker juggle two tasks?
